chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever touches a dog, let him perform wudu (ablution). The discussion concerning this report is like the discussion concerning the first report: that it is to be understood as referring to washing the hand, due to the consensus that we mentioned and the reports that we presented before; and furthermore...

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: reports; narrations used to support the interpretation
key_terms.الْإِجْمَاعِ: consensus; the juristic agreement cited as evidence
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report; the hadith under discussion
key_terms.الْيَدِ: the hand; the limb said to be washed
key_terms.غَسْلِ: washing; here referring specifically to washing the hand
key_terms.فَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ: then let him perform wudu (ablution); an imperative expression in the report
key_terms.كَلْبًا: a dog; the animal discussed in the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Does touching a dog require wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that one who touches a dog should perform wudu (ablution). In the surrounding legal discussion of al-Istibṣār, the wording is understood as referring to washing the hand rather than requiring full wudu (ablution), based on consensus and other narrations.
